subject: literature
passage: On the last night of the festival, Mei and her grandmother carried their paper lanterns down to the river. Each of the lanterns that Grandmother had folded that afternoon ______ marked with a wish written in tiny characters along its lower edge. As the lanterns drifted away on the dark water, Mei tried to guess which glowing shape held her own wish.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the verb is "Each," which is singular; "of the lanterns that Grandmother had folded" only says which ones. A singular subject needs a singular verb, and the story is told in the past tense, so "was" is correct. The singular "its lower edge" confirms that one lantern at a time is meant.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Have been" is plural, but the subject "Each" is singular.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Are" is plural, and it is also present tense in a story told in the past.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Were" is plural and seems to agree with "lanterns," but the subject is the singular "Each."
explanation.D: Correct. The singular past-tense verb "was" agrees with the singular subject "Each" and fits the past-tense story.
